overview: This file documents Chinese labor migration through Dairen and Newchwang into Japanese-controlled Manchuria from 1933 to 1937. Consular despatches, State Department memoranda, translated regulations, press extracts, and extensive statistical tables trace quarterly and annual arrivals and departures, the migrants’ provincial origins and destinations, seasonal employment patterns, wages, and remittances. The records show immigration rising sharply in 1934 before Japanese and “Manchukuo” authorities imposed labor certification, occupational allocations, and an annual quota of 440,000 people. They also describe attempts to circumvent these restrictions, problems in the official statistics, labor shortages, and the eventual suppression of migration data as military secrets in 1937. A separate departmental note concerns the 1933 Grand Manchurian Exposition.
interest: Records mass labor migration into Manchuria under Japanese rule, managed through permits and quotas until the 1937 military-secret classification.
